text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as crude oil prices surged on concerns about Saudi Arabia's pipeline closure. The East-West pipeline was damaged in a drone attack and shut down, with U.S. crude rallying to $106 and Brent crude hitting $109.51 per barrel. While Saudi officials say the closure will last only days, analysts warn that if the outage extends beyond five to seven days, oil prices could spike sharply as inventory buffers get depleted—a scenario that would directly boost revenues for a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips.

The two-week rally of 6.7% reflects a broader shift toward geopolitical risk in oil markets. Attacks from Iran-backed Houthi militants and the resulting uncertainty about Saudi infrastructure have rattled energy traders, and with oil and Treasury yields now moving in lockstep—their tightest correlation in seven years—crude has become tied to macroeconomic uncertainty as much as supply concerns.
